title: manuscript-guard revision round
description: One round of external review: what a journal's reviewers asked, what was answered, and what actually changed as a result. The internal panel (G11) records a review this project commissioned; this records one it received. The point of writing it down in the same shape as everything else is that a response is a claim like any other - 'we have revised the Methods' is checkable against whether the Methods changed, and until now nothing checked it.

decision.description: The journal's verdict, in its own vocabulary.

submitted_files.description: The manuscript as the journal received it, one digest per file. Written when the round is opened, from the version that was submitted. This is what makes a response verifiable: a point claiming the Methods were revised can be checked against whether methods.md actually differs from what went out.

id.description: As the journal names them: reviewer-1, reviewer-2, editor.

comment.description: The reviewer's words, quoted rather than paraphrased. A paraphrase is where a point quietly becomes the easier point next to it.

response.description: What the authors say back. An empty response is an unanswered point, which blocks a resubmission.

changed.description: What changed because of this point. Each entry is checked: a manuscript file must actually differ from the submitted version, and a results key must exist. A response claiming a revision that did not happen is the specific failure this whole record exists to catch.

rebutted.description: Why nothing changed. A reasoned disagreement is a legitimate answer to a reviewer and often the right one; silence is not. Recording it here is also what lets the response document say so in the author's own words rather than inventing agreement.
